transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Avalon Head of ML), Maya Chen (CTO), Luis Ortega (Infra)

Auto-summary: Quick discovery on cost per token, batching and caching levers; explore hosted vs dedicated vs private given Avalon budget target (~$30k/mo) and latency SLOs (p95 < 180ms).

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, I'm Jordan from Redwood, joined by Samira on systems. quick round intro?
[00:12] Evan: Evan Park, Head of ML at Avalon. we're evaluating options to move away from raw OpenAI spend, want better unit economics and control.
[00:20] Maya: Maya Chen here, CTO. our cifar? i mean our infra team wants predictable costs and data residency.
[00:30] Luis: Luis Ortega, infra. we run a mix of GCP and some on-prem for sensitive workloads.
[00:38] Jordan: Awesome. high level today we want to understand your usage profile, budget constraints and talk through how batching/caching and dedicated reservations change unit costs.
[00:45] Samira: Quick note - i'll probably get into some technical levers: quantization, batching sizes, KV cache hit rates, and how that translates to tokens/sec and cost.

[02:10] Evan: Current stack, we are using OpenAI for LLM calls, about 120k tokens/day average, peaks up to 1.5 million tokens/day. typical request is ~350 tokens in prompt and ~250 tokens back so about 600 tokens per request on avg. latency target for product flows is p95 < 200ms.
[02:45] Jordan: great, that's helpful. what are you seeing on cost today and what's the target?
[02:52] Maya: Right now it's around $50k/month. goal is to get down to ~$25-35k depending on accuracy tradeoffs.
[03:05] Jordan: ok, so the economics conversation will focus on per-token pricing and the levers that change that: batching, prefix/KV caching for multi-turn, model quantization and dedicated pools/reserved capacity.

[05:30] Samira: On batching - if you can tolerate a little tail latency, batching multiple requests into one kernel call gives big throughput wins. we typically see 1.5x-3x reduction in per-token cost depending on customer distribution. that's because GPU utilization goes way up.
[06:00] Luis: How about real-time chat flows? batching seems tough there.
[06:10] Samira: for strict real-time (p95 < 200ms) batching window is small; you can still micro-batch (20-50ms) and get some savings. Another big win is KV/prefix caching: for multi-turn dialogs where prefix tokens repeat, a high cache hit rate can save 30-60% of tokens served to the model.
[06:40] Evan: so you separate input tokens that need full recompute vs cached kv retrieval?
[06:47] Samira: exactly. if 40% of tokens are cached KV, your effective billed tokens drop accordingly.
[07:15] Jordan: pricing overview - hosted model per-token price varies by model size; for the call today we outlined ballpark hosted pricing vs dedicated reserved pricing. hosted is easiest to start, dedicated gets you better unit economics at scale, especially with reserved GPU pools.
[07:40] Maya: what's the break-even? when should we pick dedicated or private?
[07:46] Samira: rough rule: above ~5M tokens/month or if you need strong data isolation and committed SLAs, dedicated starts to make sense. private (VPC/on-prem) adds infra and license costs but gives full control; it's typically chosen for regulated workloads.

[09:50] Jordan: also some customers do hybrid: host non-sensitive low-latency flows, and run sensitive workloads on private. routing policies can fallback to hosted in spikes.

[11:20] Evan: can you show a sample TCO? like current OpenAI spend -> Redwood hosted -> Redwood dedicated?
[11:30] Jordan: yes we'll send a detailed spreadsheet but in rough numbers: given 1.5M tokens/day (~45M tokens/month), hosted with caching/batching could land around $0.0006-0.0012/token depending on model; dedicated reserved can push that down to $0.0002-0.0006/token with high utilization and batching. those are illustrative.
[12:05] Maya: That margin is big. what assumptions are you using for tokenization and model choice?
[12:12] Samira: assume an open 7B-ish model, int8 / q4 quantization option for throughput, and a 40-60% effective caching/hit rate and batching efficiency. if you move to higher-accuracy larger models numbers shift.

[14:00] Luis: what's the commitment term for reserved capacity? monthly, annual?
[14:05] Jordan: we offer monthly reserved or annual with better discounts. monthly gives flexibility; annual gives higher discount and capacity guarantees.
[14:25] Evan: how do you meter? is it pure billed tokens or some GPU-minutes blend for dedicated?
[14:32] Samira: hosted is per-token billed. dedicated has committed capacity pricing (GPU-hours) plus overage per-token or per-GPU-minute depending on usage profile. we expose token-level telemetry so you can attribute cost.

[16:10] Maya: on quantization - we need to validate quality drop. are you able to run evals?
[16:18] Samira: yes, we'll run a benchmark with your evaluation set and do head-to-head with different quantization profiles; we'll show latency, throughput, and quality deltas.

[18:00] Evan: we have a hard budget band of $25-35k/mo for production. with your estimates does that look achievable?
[18:12] Jordan: possible if you can push high cache hit rates and micro-batching and accept smaller model or quantization. also dedicated reserved with commit can reduce unit cost significantly, but requires commit. we should model scenarios.

[20:00] Samira: quick technical notes: cache hit rate is workload dependent. if you have high re-use of context across users (templates, system prompts, etc) caching helps. If it's highly unique free-form text, caching is minimal and batching/quantization become primary levers.
[21:10] Luis: how much engineering work to integrate prefix caching?
[21:20] Samira: very little on client side - it's mostly server-side config. Redwood supports automatic KV caching for conversational APIs and you can tune TTLs and policies. we can share integration examples.

[24:00] Evan: security side: we need SOC 2, SSO, KMS, and audit logs. private option might be required for some customers.
[24:12] Jordan: we have SOC 2, support SAML/SSO, work with KMS/HSM for key management, and provide audit logs. for private deployment we can support VPC and air-gapped on-prem. we'll send security pack.

[26:30] Maya: any limits on model variants with dedicated pools? like can we pin a quantized 13B model?
[26:40] Samira: yes you can pin model versions and quantization profiles per pool. the runtime supports kernel selection and quantized execution; some very large models have different memory requirements so we'd size GPUs accordingly.

[29:00] Evan: can we run a short benchmark? simulate our 600 tokens/request distribution and 600 rps burst?
[29:10] Samira: yes. propose a 2-hour bench: we'll run hosted and dedicated simulators with your distribution, measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, and effective cost per token.
[29:30] Jordan: we'll need sample inputs, an expected acceptance criteria and your infra contacts.

[31:20] Maya: acceptance criteria: p95 < 200ms for UI flows, effective cost <= $0.0005/token for regular flows to hit budget.
[31:35] Evan: also need guardrails for fallback - if dedicated capacity is saturated can hosted burst?
[31:42] Samira: yes we support smart routing and automatic fallback to hosted or other regions; you can set cost vs latency policies.

[34:00] Jordan: to summarize from our side: 1) send hosted vs dedicated pricing + TCO scenarios, 2) share bench harness and run 2-hr test, 3) send SOC2 & VPC docs.
[34:18] Maya: sounds good, we want pricing fast - we have an exec review on 3/10.
[34:25] Jordan: we'll prioritize getting a pricing doc to you by 3/6.

[36:00] Evan: small question - how do you attribute costs to product teams? we need token-level breakdown per route.
[36:08] Samira: Redwood Console exposes per-route token usage, per-model, and you can tag requests with team metadata; monthly exports are available.

[38:30] Luis: about on-prem private - what's the typical deployment timeline?
[38:36] Samira: on-prem deployments are 6-12 weeks depending on network and security reviews; VPC options are quicker, 2-4 weeks.

[40:00] Maya: any hidden costs we should be aware of? e.g., data egress, storage for KV cache?
[40:08] Jordan: standard infra costs for private (VMs, GPUs, network). hosted includes egress to your region; we'll call out those items explicitly in the pricing doc.

[42:10] Evan: competition - we're also talking to Anthropic and Vertex for committed pricing.
[42:18] Jordan: understood. we'll highlight benchmarking and observability differentiators.

[45:00] Jordan: ok last bit - we'll send the pricing spreadsheet, schedule the bench, and send security docs. any blockers?
[45:10] Maya: none, only exec timing.
[45:20] Evan: i'll get the sample dataset and token hist to you by Monday.
[45:28] Jordan: perfecto. thanks everyone.
[47:00] Meeting end.
